standard_prerequisites.name: Finitely generated submodules of finite free modules over a Noetherian ring are finite
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the inductive step of the counted proof (lines 17648-17651)
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the kernel of each map in the resolution finitely generated, so the next free module can be taken finite.

core_obligations: In the Noetherian case, choose a surjection from a finite free module onto M to start the resolution (proof line 17647).

At the inductive step, given an exact complex of length e, choose a surjection from a finite free module onto the kernel of the last map; this is possible because R is Noetherian, so that kernel is finitely generated (proof lines 17648-17651).
proof_roadmap: Start with a surjection onto M from a free module and iterate the construction on the kernels (proof lines 17645-17651).
In the Noetherian case keep every step finite by appealing to finite generation of the kernels (proof lines 17648-17652).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces an exact complex of free modules mapping onto any module M, and asserts that when R is Noetherian and M is finite the free modules may be taken finite (statement lines 17627-17643). The proof does not use projective covers or a minimal resolution: it builds the complex step by step, starting from a surjection onto M and then choosing a surjection onto the kernel of the last map already constructed, which can be kept finite exactly because over a Noetherian ring the kernel of a map between finite free modules is finitely generated (proof lines 17645-17652). The author states that only the Noetherian case is explained, and that explanation is the whole construction. H2.
